title: Final Project — Mini Adventure Intro

content.title: Your mission
content.summary: Write the opening screen of a text adventure using print(), strings, and variables.
content.body: You've learned print(), strings, and variables. Now put it all together. You're going to write the opening screen of a text adventure game — the kind that sets the scene before the action starts.

content.title: What to include
content.summary: A player name variable, an item variable, 4+ print() lines, and at least one + combination.
content.body:
Your adventure intro should have:
• A player name (stored in a variable)
• A weapon or item (stored in a variable)
• At least 4 print() lines that tell the start of the story
• One line that combines a variable with text using +

content.title: Example to get you started
content.summary: This is a starting point only — make the story, names, and setting completely your own.
content.body:
player = "Sam"
weapon = "Laser Sword"

print(player + " entered the dungeon.")
print("Equipped:", weapon)
print("A giant slime appeared!")

This is just a starting point — make it your own!

editorPrompt: Write the opening of a text adventure — use variables for the player and an item, and tell the story with print()
progressiveHints:
# Starter example — replace everything with your own story!
player = "Sam"
weapon = "Laser Sword"

print(player + " entered the dungeon.")
print("Equipped:", weapon)
print("A giant slime appeared!")

# Hint: Start with two variables for your character
# player = "your name here"
# item = "your item here"

player = "your name"
item = "your item"
location = "the dungeon"
print(player + " arrived at " + location + ".")

player = "Aria"
item = "Thunder Shield"
location = "the Frozen Tower"
enemy = "Ice Golem"

print(player + " arrived at " + location + ".")
print("She carried a " + item + ".")
print("A " + enemy + " blocked the path!")
print("The adventure begins...")
challenge: 🚀 Dive Deeper: Add a sidekick character with their own name variable. Have them say something in your story using print().
